page.description: Whonix editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A Debian-based anonymity system built as two virtual machines, a gateway and a workstation, that routes all traffic through Tor and isolates the browser from the host.
pros: All traffic is forced through Tor by a separate gateway VM.
The workstation cannot learn the host's IP address by design.
Runs on VirtualBox, KVM and as a Qubes OS template.
cons: It is a virtual-machine system: no plain USB install image is published.
Two VMs need more RAM than a single desktop.
The OVA appliances are for hypervisors, not for writing to a USB stick.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for Whonix; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Whonix ships as virtual-machine appliances (OVA) for VirtualBox and KVM, and as Qubes templates. Import the OVA in the hypervisor; there is no USB install image. ROMinit pins the OVA files for download and checksum only.

editions.name: LXQt
editions.description: The full Whonix desktop appliance, with the LXQt workstation and the gateway VM.
editions.usbNote: 2.5 GiB OVA appliance. Import it in VirtualBox or KVM; it is not written to a USB stick.

editions.name: CLI
editions.description: Command-line appliance without a desktop, for hosts that only need the Tor gateway and a terminal.
editions.usbNote: 1.3 GiB OVA appliance. Import it in VirtualBox or KVM; it is not written to a USB stick.
